tier1.name: Functional / Stress Hardening
reportedRegressionRequirements: Game Center selected event follows the active game video on direct tune, Next, and automatic advance
Background program refresh cannot replace or restart the active media key
Manual pause remains latched for at least 25 seconds under background refresh
Score-ribbon date browsing cannot autoplay Silver daily/weekly roundup media
Production startup contains no legacy NBA/demo seed programming
Post-first-frame playback buffering self-recovers by failing over within a bounded window instead of hanging or restarting the same clip
Launch-started YouTube media enters a tracked playback session immediately and cannot remain indefinitely in starting while iframe readiness never arrives
Every clean-window error capable of blocking certification is exported with timestamp, category/code, source, message, detail/data, and browser/runtime identity
A count-only clean-window error with no corresponding exported error record cannot independently fail Tier 1; the diagnostic mismatch remains visible as an advisory

Known transient browser media interruptions are advisory only when a later PASS playback step plus a final PLAYING/OK playback session prove automatic recovery and are labeled RECOVERED_ADVISORY in the exported certificate

Post-test exact-state restoration is advisory unless final application health is bad; cleanup health requires restored resource mode, playback ownership OK, one soundtrack audio element, a selected media item on a started board, and Game Center consistency for game-scoped media
Playback watchdog failures that prove bounded automatic failover to a different PLAYING media asset and healthy post-test state are RECOVERED_ADVISORY rather than Tier 1 blockers.

Poisoned media is blocked before native/YouTube player assignment; any already-loading matching resources are torn down locally without resetting the healthy playback engine, and certification requires zero orphaned blocked loads.
Recap tier availability is keyed to physical playback identity: the same YouTube ID/direct URL cannot be advertised as both Green Quick and Purple Extended.
Known physical duration outranks conflicting discovery-objective metadata when assigning Quick versus Extended recap tiers.

Recent NFL weekly recap playlists are dynamically discovered from the official NFL YouTube channel; missing expected preseason/regular-season week catalogs trigger a bounded refresh instead of waiting on the long-lived playlist cache.
Custom competition creation is Dev Mode only and persists server-side.
Active special events appear in both Special Events and the main selector row; completed special events remain only under Special Events.
Custom event Game Center uses the canonical /api/events/<competition>/<event>/game-center contract.
World Cup and LLWS templates require schedule review before activation.
Competition Builder editable controls isolate keyboard input from document-level playback shortcuts so typing spaces/arrows cannot control playback.
Competition creation is not reported successful until the shared server store is written and a fresh definition read-back verifies persistence.
Custom competitions are enrolled in the canonical history league registry, operator playlist crawler, and dedicated background media gap-search worker.
Schedule Auto Discover uses structured output and falls back to direct extraction of an operator-supplied official schedule URL when web search fails.

Competition Builder schedule discovery is completeness-driven: large tournaments are researched in bounded date windows, merged/deduplicated, and checked against an expected event count instead of relying on one giant model response.
Site-wide competition creation rejects zero-event schedules and rejects incomplete schedules when an expected event count is known unless a future explicit override is introduced.

Dev Mode can delete a custom competition site-wide, removing its persisted definition, history event relationships, operator playlist registrations, runtime registry entry, and history-league crawl enrollment.
World Cup and LLWS templates carry deterministic completeness targets of 104 and 38 competition games respectively.
Special Events is a permanent top-level selector control; custom special-event catalog refreshes populate that stable control instead of transiently injecting/removing the control itself.
Selecting a completed or upcoming special event while browsing outside its event date range navigates the score ribbon into the event range before rendering its games.
Custom competition score hydration subscribes to the canonical ScoreDateStore browse-date authority so special-event games render on historical event dates across normal ribbon refreshes.
Special Events dropdown content is rendered in a viewport-level portal so the horizontally scrolling league-filter container cannot clip its menu.
Custom competition date hydration rebuilds the verified-media lookup used by score-card playback after schedule/media enter ScoreDateStore.
Custom operator playlist registrations are durably saved before asynchronous playlist crawl begins; existing custom competitions re-enroll media sources on server startup.
Custom event-media responses force canonical competition/event identity from the event relationship and lazily repair matching unassigned custom source media.
Competition Builder persists an explicit participant artwork strategy; the FIFA World Cup defaults to country flags while future competitions can choose team logos, provided artwork, auto, or none.
Competition Builder startup cannot recursively resolve the Special Events portal; the stable Special Events menu is read from the application DOM and may then be portaled to the viewport.
Competition Builder startup exposes READY/ERROR boot state and surfaces a visible Special Events warning if initialization fails instead of silently removing all custom-competition UI.
The 4.6.4 custom competition runtime bridge, participant artwork strategy, canonical custom-media identity repair, and verified-media lookup rebuild remain required in 4.6.6.

Special-event main-row eligibility is evaluated against the score ribbon browse date, so a historical tournament is treated as an active league while browsing dates inside its event window even after the real-world event has completed.
Special Events dropdown presentation does not expose internal event-count bookkeeping and instead presents a clean event identity plus date-relative active/completed status.

Past tournament bracket placeholders are reconciled to actual played participants/results from authoritative sources while preserving each canonical event ID so existing media associations remain intact.
Custom competition playback exposes explicit away/home display-name strings alongside rich participant objects and artwork so legacy title paths cannot render [object Object].
Participant artwork strategy is preserved through custom schedule hydration and Game Center; the FIFA World Cup AUTO/template strategy resolves country participants to flag artwork.
Tournament ingestion is state-aware: matches dated today or earlier use actual realized participants/results, while future bracket placeholders remain only until official participants are determined.
The 2026 FIFA World Cup uses ESPN fifa.world as the deterministic primary participant/result authority.
Provider match IDs are stored separately while canonical Sports Big Board event IDs remain unchanged.
Ongoing tournaments resolve future bracket slots as soon as both actual participants are officially known.
Custom soccer competitions use the standard ESPN soccer Game Center structure with scoring plays, team stats, player/lineup sections, commentary timeline, venue/status and soccer completeness rules.
If ESPN soccer Game Center cannot be loaded, the generic custom Game Center remains a non-breaking fallback.
History Audit exposes a Statistics tab with per-competition game/media coverage and includes dynamically registered special events.
Media Playlists dynamically exposes registered special-event competitions alongside MLB, NFL, NBA, NHL, EPL, and MLS.
Every competition can explicitly reprocess media from the Media Playlists or Statistics surfaces without deleting existing verified media.
Built-in league media reprocessing reopens the normal source-enrichment ledger so completed source checks become eligible again.
Special-event media reprocessing force-crawls every enabled operator playlist and runs canonical event-media association repair.
When tournament participant/result reconciliation changes an event from bracket identity to realized teams, registered competition playlists are force-crawled again automatically.
History Audit, Silver, playlist-management, and recovery league selectors are populated from the live competition/media registry rather than a six-league hard-coded list.
Completed custom soccer events normalize provider terminal states such as FT to canonical FINAL before score-ribbon playback eligibility is evaluated.
A past custom soccer event with official scores cannot remain canonically SCHEDULED; it is exposed as FINAL while preserving the provider status separately.
Future and live custom soccer matches are never forced to FINAL merely because a score is present.
World Cup verified GAME media associated to a completed match remains eligible for the normal score-ribbon play arrow and click-to-play path.
Existing persisted World Cup FT/stale-completion rows are normalized on schedule reads and revisited by background result reconciliation without changing canonical event IDs.
Historical score-ribbon dates remain database-first: FIND RECAP and external discovery are gated until normalized catalog hydration and date-scoped association repair complete.
Historical ribbon reads re-prove already-downloaded orphaned or quarantined GAME assets against the requested date before external media discovery begins.

Schedule/provider event-id changes that are proven to be the same league/date/team/time matchup are stored as aliases to the existing canonical event instead of breaking historical media relationships.
Bulk historical ribbon media is exposed under canonical event keys and all proven provider aliases while the underlying source-to-game relationship remains singular.
Historical date switching is generation-safe: a late database hydration from a previously browsed date cannot launch recap search or repaint the current date.
Historical diagnostics distinguish database association readiness from genuine no-media state and report games checked, ribbon-ready games, and remaining missing games.
Competition Builder Identity exposes an Event Icon selector beside Sport with a prepopulated reusable icon library.
eventIcon is persisted as competition metadata and each Special Events dropdown row renders that event-specific icon with a sport-aware fallback for older competitions.

The 2026 Little League Baseball World Series template remains completeness-gated at 38 competition games, uses August 19-30, 2026, and points schedule discovery at the official Little League tournament schedule.
The LLWS template defaults to baseball, the baseball event icon, ESPN league slug llb, provider sport baseball, and the standard baseball Game Center profile.

2026 LLWS played games use ESPN baseball/llb as a deterministic participant/result authority while canonical Sports Big Board event IDs remain stable and unresolved future bracket participants remain placeholders only until official.

Custom baseball special events with an ESPN provider mapping use the standard baseball Game Center structure including inning linescore, team stats, player sections, timeline/scoring plays when provided, with the generic custom Game Center retained as a non-breaking fallback.

LLWS automatically inherits special-event playlist enrollment, Statistics reporting, media reprocessing, historical database-first hydration, schedule aliases, and date-scoped media reassociation from the existing generic competition contracts.
Competition Builder exposes a COPY TEMPLATE JSON control that copies the canonical generic special-event schedule import structure without generating Sports Big Board event IDs.

The generic schedule import structure supports rich away/home participant objects with name, displayName, group, abbreviation, and aliases plus scheduledAt, scores, provider IDs, gameNumber, round/stage, venue, city/country, and sourceUrl.
Custom competition media sources can persist optional required/excluded playlist title phrases; required phrases are OR-based and any excluded phrase rejects the candidate before GAME association.

Historical Database Game Media Playlists exposes the same required/excluded playlist title phrases for existing special-event sources and rule changes trigger a force recrawl without deleting existing source media.
Custom-event media association uses imported participant aliases, abbreviations, groups, and region identities as additional event-match evidence while preserving canonical event IDs.
LLWS template media matching defaults the Green source required phrase to Full Game Highlights while remaining operator-editable and reusable for other competitions.
Special-event operator playlist association compares every title-rule-eligible GAME asset against the full competition schedule before publication date can narrow candidates.
Required/excluded playlist title phrases are evaluated before tournament-wide event association so miscellaneous clips remain SOURCE_MEDIA and do not compete with configured game recaps.
Participant names, aliases, abbreviations, groups, and regions remain valid matchup evidence across the full competition candidate set.

Repeated participant matchups are resolved only by stronger provider identity, explicit title game number/date, or bounded publication-date proximity; unresolved ambiguity remains orphaned rather than guessed.
Already-downloaded special-event operator playlist orphans are re-associated from SOURCE_MEDIA at backend startup without redownloading or deleting source assets.
Future special-event playlist crawls persist both the internal operator playlist ID and provider YouTube playlist ID so multi-playlist title rules remain deterministic.
Special-event Statistics WITH MEDIA uses durable playable EVENT_MEDIA relationships that the score ribbon can actually consume instead of broad source-catalog availability.
REPROCESS MEDIA uses the tournament-wide special-event crawler so orphan counts and ribbon-ready game coverage converge on the same durable association truth.
Special-event media association derives media-facing geographic identities from imported participant aliases, including the final state/country component of City, State/Country location aliases.
Imported participant group labels ending in Region contribute a media alias without the Region suffix while one-character abbreviations are excluded from title matching.

Special-event media titles containing public state/country identities such as Alabama, Ohio, Washington, Nicaragua, Czechia, Japan, Canada, South Korea, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Iowa can match the canonical schedule participant objects without rewriting those schedule objects.
Common recap abbreviations and equivalents such as PA/NJ, DR/Dominican Republic, Curacao/Curaçao, and Czechia/Czech Republic are normalized as media aliases.
The special-event tournament crawler attempts a deterministic two-sided SPECIAL_EVENT_TITLE_ALIAS_PAIR match before falling back to the generic event matcher.
Existing special-event SOURCE_MEDIA orphans are automatically re-associated after the v4.6.14 media-alias layer installs; canonical event IDs and existing EVENT_MEDIA remain unchanged.

Persistence accepts a deterministic special-event proof only when it is produced by the internal SBB special-event matcher, names the exact target league/event/canonical key, carries both title-side aliases, and has confidence of at least 0.90.
A SPECIAL_EVENT_TITLE_ALIAS_PAIR proof is not reinterpreted by the older canonical-team-only event matcher during the same put_event_media write.
Existing TITLE_TEAM_PAIR_CONFLICT quarantines can be released to ASSIGNED only after the exact special-event alias proof is re-established for the same canonical event.
A pre-proven special-event asset never steals an asset that is already ASSIGNED to another canonical event; the new candidate remains MULTI_EVENT_CANDIDATE_ENCOUNTER.
Ordinary built-in league and generic event-media persistence continues to use the original fail-closed event matcher with no bypass.
Relationship repair may run the normal generic revalidation, but still-valid persisted internal special-event proofs are restored before repair completes.
v4.6.15 automatically re-associates existing special-event SOURCE_MEDIA after installation so previously quarantined Full Game Highlights do not require playlist deletion or redownload.

Pre-proven special-event persistence creates or refreshes the canonical-event parent and validates both canonical-event and source-media foreign-key parents on the same SQLite transaction before writing history_event_media.
Special-event media association is consolidated into an explicit SOURCE -> ELIGIBLE -> CANDIDATES -> MATCHED -> PERSISTED -> PLAYABLE pipeline with per-asset audit output.

For custom competitions, the persistent custom-competition registry event is the participant-identity authority; normalized history/provider refreshes may update runtime metadata but may not erase imported aliases, groups, abbreviations, or official gameNumber.
Special-event participant crosswalks derive stable media-facing identities from imported team names, aliases, locations, groups, regions, and safe abbreviations before media association.
Special-event association prefers a unique official gameNumber when media names one, then evaluates the full tournament using participant alias pairs and deterministic repeated-matchup tie breakers.
REASSOCIATE is database-only and never revisits a provider; RECRAWL SOURCES is the only operator action that performs provider/network collection before reassociation.
Association Audit exposes every source asset's eligibility result, candidate count, selected canonical event, association method, persistence state, playability, and rejection reason.

Once a special-event media asset is durably assigned, its normalized source scope is GAME with SPECIAL_EVENT_CANONICAL_ASSOCIATION so Statistics and historical ribbon playback read the same EVENT_MEDIA truth.
Special-event WITH MEDIA means at least one durable playable assigned EVENT_MEDIA relationship, never merely a source candidate or broad catalog match.

v4.6.16 migrates LLWS2026 to two explicit sources without recreating the schedule: LittleLeague.org Game Recaps as Green and the ESPN 2026 LLWS YouTube playlist as Purple with Full Game Highlights title eligibility.

The WEB_RECAP_INDEX source adapter collects only Recap: video pages, preserves LittleLeague.org as the official external source, promotes direct MP4/HLS media when exposed, and records Brightcove embed metadata when direct media is not available.

For special events, custom-competition registry events are the identity authority; provider/history rows may enrich runtime metadata but cannot replace imported participant aliases, groups, abbreviations, or official gameNumber.

Once v4.6.16 proves a special-event title by official gameNumber or a deterministic two-sided participant-alias pair, persistence writes the normalized history_event_media relationship directly and does not run the legacy canonical-team-only matcher a second time.

LLWS source migration re-reads the full persisted competition definition after save_competition because catalog rows intentionally omit events; startup reassociation therefore always retains the imported identity crosswalk.
LittleLeague.org recap pages preserve publication metadata when available so repeated participant matchups can use the same bounded chronology tie-breaker as YouTube playlist media.
Special-event orphan counts mean SOURCE_MEDIA assets with no durable ASSIGNED EVENT_MEDIA relationship; playable coverage is reported separately from association coverage.
If both event-family and collection-family integrity drift are present, startup repair forces both families before the hard post-repair audit.
The v4.6.16 relationship-routing correction installs synchronously during sbb import so it is active before server.py executes the backend startup repair gate.

Competition Registry 2.0 is the backend authority for competition existence and retains the COMPETITIONS mutable-mapping, catalog(), and enabled_ids() compatibility contracts used by server.py and Competition Builder.

Built-in leagues and dynamically-created leagues/special events share the same observable CompetitionCatalog; direct COMPETITIONS[id] registration emits REGISTER/UPDATE events and deletion emits UNREGISTER.
A dynamically-created competition is automatically enrolled in HISTORY_LEAGUES and Day State through registry events without a hard-coded league branch or backend redeploy.

Day State Engine persists precomputed day snapshots in day-state.sqlite3 and projects the existing canonical _history_day_score_rows, _history_day_ribbon_plans, and _history_day_score_inventory_complete outputs instead of introducing a second scoring/media truth.

The existing /api/history/ribbon contract is served cache-first from Day State using scoreRowsByLeague and eventPlans, so the main Big Board reads a precomputed backend read model while retaining the previous handler as failure fallback.
Day State continuously warms today and nearby dates, prioritizes operator/browser focus dates, and uses short freshness windows for current/live days with long historical freshness windows.
The browser prepaints selected dates from /api/day-state and ingests the same compact catalog plans used by established ribbon logic; legacy provider/date loaders remain recovery/freshness fallbacks.
Historical Database Audit exposes DAY STATE and BACKEND REGISTRY operator views showing snapshot freshness and whether dynamically-created competitions are enrolled in History and Day State.

Backend Registry and Day State state survive frontend reloads; dynamic competition definitions remain sourced from the persistent Competition Builder store and are replayed into Competition Registry 2.0 on backend startup.
Day State facts are derived from the same snapshot as ribbon scores/media, including game counts, live/final counts, playable-game counts, and represented competitions.

The catalog integrity metric silverGameLeaks means an ASSIGNED event-media relationship whose current normalized source scope is not GAME; it is an event-link integrity condition and remains owned by event relationship repair.
Special-event media code does not monkeypatch HistoryRepository.repair_relationships or override the core server startup repair-family plan.
A persisted pre-proven special-event relationship may be restored after relationship repair only when the source asset's current normalized scope is GAME.

If a newer media classifier changes a proof-bearing source asset from GAME to DAY_LEAGUE, WEEK_LEAGUE, ROUND_LEAGUE, or another collection scope, pre-proven restoration must not resurrect its quarantined event relationship.
Trusted special-event persistence checks the normalized source scope before writing an ASSIGNED event link and fails closed with NON_GAME_SCOPE_PREPROVEN_REJECTED when that scope is not GAME.
The consolidated v4.6.16 canonical special-event persistence path may explicitly persist a deterministically proven game asset as scope GAME with reason SPECIAL_EVENT_CANONICAL_ASSOCIATION.

tier2.name: Extended Soak
requirements: At least 90% of expected 15-second telemetry samples are captured across the full soak window
No telemetry gap exceeds 2.5 sample intervals
Playback currentTime advances while state is playing; sustained no-progress beyond 45 seconds fails
Native video play-request acknowledgment is bounded so a pending HTMLMediaElement.play() Promise cannot delay first-frame recovery
Sustained buffering beyond 45 seconds fails
Timed-out game-transition calls are evidence and must recover within 20 seconds; only unrecovered transition timeouts fail the soak
Media decode/provider failures must self-recover to another playable selection rather than strand unattended playback
No playback ownership invariant violation
No same-media currentTime restart or same-media reselection regression
Game Center remains tied to game-scoped active media
Workers remain healthy during periodic platform snapshots
No milestone clean-window errors
No excessive JavaScript heap growth when browser heap telemetry is available

tier3.name: Controlled Chaos / Recovery
requirements: Background rerank storm preserves active playback
Aborted concurrent request storm recovers
Expected invalid-route failure is isolated from playback
Standby-player disruption does not disturb active playback
Resource-mode turbulence restores the original mode
Repeated game transitions preserve Game Center ownership
Manual pause survives concurrent API pressure
Post-chaos clean recovery window is healthy
Game Center provider 429 opens a bounded scheduler circuit and cancels queued background amplification
Tier 3 chaos evidence remains exportable through the post-chaos recovery reset
Timing-only WARN evidence remains visible and advisory; only failed assertions or failed recovery gates block Tier 3 certification

baseline: v4.7.0 Competition Registry 2.0 + Day State Engine, with corrected normalized relationship ownership: silverGameLeaks is an event-link scope violation, core server.py owns repair routing, and legacy pre-proven special-event links cannot be restored after the normalized classifier says the asset is no longer GAME.
